summary: The board-specific logic this core adds is organised around MAME's konamigx driver, not the GX board. The interrupt and DMA-timing block repeats MAME's m_gx_syncen / m_gx_rdport1_3 bookkeeping test for test. The ESC is MAME's generate_sprites C laid out as a state machine. The sprite colour/priority callback, the solid/shadow split and the mixer's sort key are copied from konamigx_mixer and its helpers, including MAME's per-game hacks (primode 4/5, spri_min, the Lethal Enforcer +0x20). The only parts that look like hardware are vendored jotego chip models (the K053252 counter chain, the K053246 per-line scan and DMA). Even there, the K053246's DMA ordering and enable were changed with GX_ORDER/GX_DMA_ALWAYS so they behave like MAME's live, RAM-order draw.

findings.signal: IRQ/DMA logic transliterated from MAME callbacks
findings.note: These registers mirror MAME's member variables: wrport1_1, rdport1_3 (reset 0xfc), and syncen updated with syncen |= data&0x1f when bit 7 is set. The checks are the same expressions: (wrport1_1 & 0x84)==0x84 || syncen[2], then clear syncen bit 2 and rdport1_3 &= ~0x82. A fixed countdown (dma_len) stands in for MAME's dmadelay timer, not the K053246's own DMA busy signal.

findings.signal: ESC = generate_sprites as a state machine
findings.note: States S_H0..S_H11 read the header at adr+4/+8/+12/+14/+20/+22/+24/+26/+18/+16 in MAME's order into glob_x, glob_y, zoom_x, color_mask, color_val, color_set and color_rotate. The piece loop has MAME's idx==0xffff jump, its -256..544 / -256..512 clipping, the (flip^glob_f)|pri word and the return at 256 sprites. MAME's software protection stand-ins (fantjour DMA, type-4 Xilinx commands) are implemented in the same way.

findings.signal: Sprite callback copied from konamigx_precache_registers / combine_c18 / decode_objcolor
findings.note: The coregmask table {f,e,c,8,0}, coregshift = 4+i clamped at 4, the wrport2 bit 2/3 c18 masking, opon = oinprion<<8|0xff and ocb = (ocblk&7)<<10 match MAME's helper functions value for value. The vrcbk bank case is MAME's m_k053247_vrcbk[4].

findings.signal: konamigx_mixer object-pool rules and hacks per sprite
findings.note: The shadow split (shadow!=1 || objset1&0x20 gives partial, otherwise full shadow if shadowon[0]), shadowon from deltas outside +/-7, zcode inverted by OPSET bit 4, spri from OPSET bit 5 or shdpri[], primode 4's 'k&0x3000 || k==0x0800' filter and the primode 4/5 spri_min clamp (which MAME marks HACK) are reproduced as written.

findings.signal: Mixer ranks by MAME's objpool sort key
findings.note: Each source gets the key {pri, class, zcode, sprite index, sub} and the smallest wins. That is MAME's software draw-order word {priority, zcode, offset, shadow mode} applied per pixel. Shadow codes under SHD PRI SEL conditions 1/2 take MAME's deferred-shadow path. The pixel pipeline itself is FPGA engineering; the decision rule it carries out is MAME's.

findings.signal: MAME table arithmetic and per-game hacks in the blender
findings.note: The shadow colour is cut to 5 bits and re-expanded the way pal5bit does, the deltas are clamped as set_shadow_dRGB32 does, and the alpha level comes from set_alpha_level with invert_alpha. Layer C gets PRIINP_3+0x20 under primode -1, which is MAME's 'Lethal Enforcer hack'. These are emulator conventions, not K054338/K055555 internals.

findings.signal: Tilemap computed in MAME coordinates with MAME's set_layer_offs fudges
findings.note: The renderer works out MAME's modulo expression with a restoring-divide state machine and subtracts per-game offsets -2/0/2/3 (+1 for dragoonj), which are MAME's software corrections. Its render window is MAME's visarea columns (vis_x0 24/40), not the K054157's own counters.

findings.signal: Raster re-expressed as MAME bitmap coordinates
findings.note: From the K053252 blanking it derives hdump/vdump so that bitmap column = hdump-0x58 and row = vdump-0x100. Every downstream block (tilemap rd_x, mixer bx/by, sprite HOFFSET/VOFFSET) is indexed in MAME's screen bitmap space rather than by the chips' own H/V counts.

findings.signal: Chip behaviour overridden to match MAME
findings.note: The vendored K053246 DMA sorts sprites into priority slots and copies only when DMAEN is set. With GX_ORDER=1 it copies in RAM order, and GX_DMA_ALWAYS ignores DMAEN, so the order of sprites in front is settled per pixel by MAME's {zcode, pri} key instead. The chip's own behaviour is switched off in favour of how MAME draws the live list.

findings.signal: Per-set table of MAME machine-config constants
findings.note: Board behaviour is chosen by MAME's per-game switches: primode 4/5/-1, the K055673 dx offsets, the esc_src/esc_count arguments of the *_esc callbacks, and the gameDefs 'special' numbers (prot4, fj_dma, guns). These configure emulator hacks; they are not board straps or PAL differences.

findings.signal: Vendored K053252 as counter chain with chip cells
findings.note: The CRTC is built from loadable counters (jtframe_count_ld), edge latches for INT1/INT2 with acknowledge clears, and blanking compares named after die cells (j31). It is programmed by the game's register writes. This is chip-level structure, but it comes from a vendored jotego model.

At each HS the sprite engine walks the object table in sub-steps (even/odd word reads, zoom, in-zone test, then per-16-pixel draw requests), as the chip scans per line, and feeds a line-buffer drawer. This is a hardware-style pipeline, though here it carries MAME-derived ordering and callbacks.

findings.signal: Memory map, ROM readback, FPGA plumbing
findings.note: The address decode and the ROM readback windows must match any correct emulator, though they reuse MAME's handler names (esc_w, konamigx_tilebank_w, m_rom_half). The ROM cache, line-buffer RAM split, draw queue and SDRAM handshakes are resource choices.
